name: Charley Yang
tagline: Korean-American singer, songwriter and producer. Four names, two personas, one guy who made most of it himself on an iPad.

facts.v: Shrewsbury, Massachusetts — Oak Middle School, Shrewsbury High
Born Chandol, changed to Charley at age 7
Ukulele, guitar, electric guitar, piano, cello, vocals
Alt-pop, bedroom pop, indie rock, folk, hyperpop, emo rap
Self-released → Mercury / Republic → AWAL → Chandol Productions
Twenty One Pilots, Milky Chance, Dominic Fike

bio: Charley Yang was born in Daegu, South Korea on August 25, 2002, and grew up in Shrewsbury, Massachusetts, where he went to Oak Middle School and Shrewsbury High. He was put into classical training from about the age of four, quit, and did not come back to writing his own music until high school. He confirmed his birthplace years later, on stage at the Seoul Jazz Festival.

He started uploading to SoundCloud in March 2019 under the handle ookbaba, nearly two years before anything of his reached streaming. Then in 2020 his brother showed him TikTok. He was eighteen and introverted and worried about what his friends would say, so he built a persona to hide inside: BoyWithUke, an opaque face shield with two big LED eyes, a ukulele, and a series called Minute-Long Songs.

The series blew up, and he kept pace with it himself — Melatonin Dreams and Fever Dreams in 2021, the Trouvaille and Faded EPs around them, all self-released, all produced at home in GarageBand on an iPad. “Two Moons” went Gold. Then “Toxic” spent thirty-one straight weeks climbing Billboard’s Alternative Airplay chart to number one and went Platinum, and he was no longer a bedroom act.

Mercury and Republic signed him in late 2021. Serotonin Dreams followed in May 2022 with “IDGAF” featuring blackbear, which also went Platinum, plus guest spots from mxmtoon and Powfu. He put out “Sick of U” with Oliver Tree, opened for AJR on the OK Orchestra tour, played a Roblox concert, made Billboard’s Emerging Artists and 21 Under 21, and got an iHeartRadio Best New Artist nomination — all with nobody knowing his face.

The mask stopped working. He has said it was hurting his personal life, his creativity and his mental and physical health, that he could not see the crowd from the stage, and that he had simply outgrown it. On October 9, 2023 he took it off at the end of the “Homesick” video, and the next day posted his face and his name on Instagram.

Burnout came in November 2024, written through the end of a four-year relationship and a split from his label, released independently through AWAL, and announced in advance as the last BoyWithUke album. He called it the most himself the persona could manage. BoyWithUke: B Sides in September 2025 emptied the vault of scrapped songs and shut the chapter for good.

Then he took his own name back. Mercurial, the first chandol album, arrived July 10, 2026 on his own imprint: twelve songs in thirty-one minutes, mixed by Jeremie Inhaber with live drums from Aaron Sterling, written start to finish by Yang, and described by him as wandering around his own memory palace. A seven-city headline run followed, then a tour documentary, then the surprise EP and uh in October.

nameStory.intro: Chandol is not a stage name he invented. It is the name he was born with, and getting back to it took about seventeen years.

steps.t: His Korean given name, and his legal name from birth.
Legally changed around age seven, after the family settled in Massachusetts, because people in America found Chandol odd and it drew attention.
The handle on his first SoundCloud uploads, before the mask or the ukulele brand existed.
The masked TikTok persona. Five studio albums, three EPs, two Platinum singles, and five years of nobody knowing his face.
Announced in November 2024 alongside Burnout as what came next. New accounts and the “TELL ME ABOUT YOURSELF” teaser appeared in 2026, and the name went on an actual record with Mercurial that July.
His own imprint. Mercurial and and uh are both released through it, which is also why the credits read producer: chandol, songwriter: Charley Yang.

notes: He has said naming the project after his Korean name was a way of accepting where he comes from, and that he feels disconnected from his Korean roots and does not know his extended family in Korea well.
Spelled lowercase as chandol on releases, the same way boywithuke was styled on SoundCloud.
The old name was not quietly dropped: he announced the end of BoyWithUke before Burnout came out, then posted a comedy video in November 2024 in which he interviewed himself about the change.

faq.q: Is chandol the same person as BoyWithUke?
faq.a: Yes. Same guy, Charley Yang. BoyWithUke was the masked persona from 2020 to 2025; chandol is what he releases under now.

faq.q: When did he start using the name chandol?
faq.a: He announced it in November 2024 around Burnout, set up chandol accounts and teased the project in early 2026, and first released music under it on May 22, 2026 with “Breakfast in Bed.” The name itself is his original legal name from birth.

faq.q: Why did he change his name?
faq.a: Chandol is his Korean name, and was his legal name until it was changed to Charley at about age seven because it stood out in America. Going back to it was his way of accepting where he comes from.

faq.q: Why did he wear a mask?
faq.a: He was eighteen, introverted, and worried what his friends would think. He has also said anonymity helped his creativity and kept attention on the songs rather than his face.

faq.q: Why did he take it off?
faq.a: He said it was hurting his personal life, his creativity and his mental and physical health, that he could not see the audience on stage, and that he had outgrown it.
He has said so. Burnout was announced as the last album under the name, and BoyWithUke: B Sides in 2025 cleared out the unreleased material to close it.

faq.q: Is he signed to a label?
faq.a: No. He was with Mercury and Republic from late 2021, left around Burnout, which came out through AWAL, and now releases through his own imprint, Chandol Productions.
“Toxic.” It climbed Billboard’s Alternative Airplay chart for 31 straight weeks to No. 1 and is certified Platinum.
